author: Nayan Seth
description:
China’s latest export controls and sanctions against American companies in response to recent US measures underscore Beijing’s expanding economic toolkit and its growing willingness to deploy it, according to analysts.
“The multiple actions that China undertook underscore the breadth and depth of China’s retaliatory toolbox,” said Wendy Cutler, the senior vice-president at the Asia Society Policy Institute.
She added that Beijing’s latest response stood in “sharp contrast” to its “ability and...
title: China’s retaliation against US shows depth of its trade war strategy, analysts say

author: Amber Wang
description:
The People’s Liberation Army is just a year away from its centenary goals in its evolution into a “world-class” fighting force. In this part of a series, Amber Wang looks at the growing influence of artificial intelligence in combat and the private firms stepping into the area.
Roughly two months before the United States launched air strikes on Iran, a little-known Chinese technology company was watching an unusual pattern emerge on its screens.
Drawing on open-source intelligence and artificial...
title: China’s Palantir? Private tech firms surge into defence AI, aiming to match US giants

author: Lijia Zhang
description:
China’s national childcare subsidy is an encouraging acknowledgement of a simple truth: raising children is expensive.
This year, the central government allocated 99.9 billion yuan (US$14.8 billion) to the programme, which provides families with 3,600 yuan annually for each child under three. According to state media, the families of more than 25 million babies have received the subsidy as of last month.
For families struggling with the cost of nappies, milk, clothes and healthcare, any...
title: China’s baby boom depends on gender equality, not cash handouts

author: Igor Patrick
description:
Brazil intends to sell yuan bonds in China every year rather than once, a senior Brazilian treasury official said on Wednesday, in a plan that would make the Chinese currency a permanent fixture of its external debt.
The debut is expected before the end of the year and is small enough that the government is not relying on the proceeds, with external debt at four per cent of the federal stock.
Francisco Segundo, deputy secretary for public debt at the National Treasury, told a webinar hosted by...
title: Brazil to become regular borrower in China, treasury official says

author: Han Li
description:
Even as Congress remains divided over the latest US defence bill, lawmakers in both parties remain united on one issue: China.
The National Defence Authorisation Act (NDAA), which sets US defence policy and authorises military spending each year, reflects a broad bipartisan consensus on expanding Washington’s military, technological and economic rivalry with Beijing.
While the House and Senate versions differ on a number of provisions, both include new measures on Taiwan, artificial...
title: China competition looms large in 2027 US defence bill

author: Fan Chen
description:
Washington has reopened discussions on billions in arms sales to Taiwan, casting a shadow over a leaders’ summit just weeks away – a meeting already burdened by bilateral trade frictions.
US President Donald Trump is expected to submit a US$14 billion Taiwan arms package to the US Congress soon, according to senior Republican lawmaker Michael McCaul on Tuesday.
“I am confident the president will forward soon another package to Congress with an additional US$14 billion in critical military...
title: US hawks push Trump on multibillion-dollar Taiwan arms deal ahead of Xi summit

author: Laura Zhou
description:
Beijing has been urged to create its own law to protect its underwater fibre-optic cables, as global fears grow over sabotage of critical ocean infrastructure.
The recommendation by Shanghai Maritime University law professor Guo Ran comes amid growing threats to the undersea cables that carry about 99 per cent of global intercontinental data, including in critical chokepoints such as the Red Sea and the Baltic Sea.
As a major coastal state and a key investor in the Digital Silk Road, China has a...
title: China urged to protect underwater cables amid growing fears of ocean sabotage

author: Dannie Peng
description:
A former senior Chinese defence official has been sentenced to 10 years in prison for accepting over 43 million yuan (US$6.3 million) in bribes, as China’s anti-corruption drive continues it sweep through the military sector.
Zhang Jianhua, former deputy head of China’s State Administration of Science, Technology and Industry for National Defence, was sentenced on Wednesday by the Dazhou Intermediate People’s Court in Sichuan province, according to state news agency Xinhua.
The court was told...
title: China jails retired defence tech overseer for 10 years in US$6.3m corruption case

author: Gabriel Dominguez
description:
Japan’s efforts to build a long-range capability to strike Chinese warships reached a milestone last week as flight testing began for the air-launched variant of its upgraded Type 12 anti-ship missile, a weapon with a reported range of about 1,000km (620 miles).
Photographs taken by aviation enthusiasts on July 30 at Gifu airbase in central Japan show a Mitsubishi F-2B fighter carrying two inert examples of the missile beneath its wings, marking the first public confirmation of a flight...
title: Japan tests long-range Type 12 missile as counterstrike capability against China grows

author: Liu Zhen,Amber Wang
description:
The People’s Liberation Army has unveiled the first official footage showing a nuclear-capable air-launched ballistic missile, the Jing Lei-1, mounted on an H-6N bomber in combat-ready status during a joint anti-ship exercise.
The strategic bomber was seen in flight, carrying a massive missile under its belly, in the final episode of the documentary Securing Victory, which has been airing on state broadcaster CCTV as part of the celebrations of the PLA’s 99th anniversary on August 1.
While CCTV...
title: Why did a Chinese bomber carry a nuclear-capable missile in an anti-ship exercise?

author: Holly Chik
description:
The underwater cables that play a vital role supporting the international digital economy are increasingly vulnerable to attack from low-cost drones, Chinese military researchers have warned.
They said the seabed had long been viewed as a strategic “blind spot” due to the difficulty of exploration and the high cost of controlling it, but was becoming a “new arena for great power rivalry”.
“The barrier to entry for undersea warfare is lowering,” Shi Guanglei and Shi Haiming from the National...
title: PLA scientists say submarine cables carrying 99% of global data could be ‘easy target’

author: Carol Yang
description:
Bangkok’s Suvarnabhumi Airport has apologised for “inappropriate behaviour” following backlash over an employee making a slant-eyed gesture towards reportedly disruptive Chinese nationals.
The apology came soon after Thai authorities insisted that individual clashes would not harm bilateral relations.
In a statement on Tuesday night, airport management expressed regret over the “inappropriate behaviour and expressions of the personnel concerned”, noting that disciplinary action had been taken...
title: Bangkok airport apologises after clash with Chinese tourists at boarding gate

author: Khushboo Razdan
description:
US President Donald Trump on Tuesday accused China of fuelling the growing nationwide backlash against AI data centres, claiming Beijing is promoting resistance because the United States is pulling ahead in the global artificial intelligence race.
“A big part of it is China,” Trump told Fox News during a California visit focused on the economy ahead of the midterm elections in November.
“Look, whoever wins the AI race is going to win AI. It’s bigger than the internet. It’s bigger than maybe...
title: ‘China doesn’t want these built’: Trump claims Beijing is behind AI data centre protests

author: Meredith Chen
description:
An All Nippon Airways passenger jet took evasive action after coming close to a government inspection aircraft near Tokyo’s Haneda airport on Tuesday, in the latest aviation safety incident at the airport since a deadly runway collision in 2024.
According to Japanese media reports, ANA flight NH968 from Shanghai was approaching the airport at around 6am on Tuesday when its traffic collision avoidance system (TCAS) was activated, warning of a potential collision risk with another aircraft.
The...
title: Narrow escape: how ANA flight from Shanghai avoided a collision at Tokyo airport

author: Nayan Seth
description:
Most Americans believe the Donald Trump administration has been unable to achieve its war objectives against Iran, according to a Marquette Law School poll released on Wednesday, as negotiations continue to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and end five months of hostilities.
A striking 88 per cent of respondents said the US had not achieved its goals in the war with Iran, up seven percentage points from April, while only 12 per cent believed it had met its objectives, down from 21 per cent.
The poll...
title: Most Americans say US has not achieved war goals in Iran, survey finds

author: Holly Chik
description:
Much of the global debate on Chinese military power focuses on hardware but a vital part of the modernisation process is in the niche field of software verification.
Wang Ji, a computer science researcher at the National University of Defence Technology (NUDT), is mentoring a new generation of scientists to treat the software code in national defence systems with the same precision as doctors diagnosing patients.
After losing both legs to a life-threatening emergency, Wang, 56, has stayed at the...
title: How an amputee Chinese scientist is fortifying the country’s military software

author: Alcott Wei
description:
The sweeping anti-corruption drive in China’s military appears to have cleared the way for a new batch of officers to quietly assume de facto leadership of key People’s Liberation Army bodies.
According to a South China Morning Post analysis of official insignia and protocol seating from state media coverage of recent meetings, dozens of fresh commanders have stepped into the roles of their ousted predecessors, positioning them to lead the world’s largest standing army.
Many have assumed major...
title: Who are the officers filling the big shoes left behind in PLA anti-corruption drive?
